transcript: AI Avatar: Priya, tumhare bhai ne party mein kya kiya? [Priya, what did your brother do at the party?] Human: He cut my nose in front of everyone. AI Avatar: Kya? Usne sach mein naak kaat di? Isse 'He embarrassed me' bolte hain. Angrez sunte toh darr jaate. [What? Did he really cut your nose? This is called 'He embarrassed me'. If English speakers heard that, they'd get scared.] Human: Ufff! Meri yeh direct translation wali aadat kab jayegi? [Ugh! When will this habit of direct translation go away?] AI Avatar: Jab tum Speakeasy app download karogi. Main ek AI teacher hoon. Tum 100 baar aise galtiyan karogi, main 100 baar bina hanse sudharungi. [When you download the Speakeasy app. I am an AI teacher. You will make such mistakes 100 times, I will correct you 100 times without laughing.] Human: Yeh hui na baat! Main abhi try karti hoon. [That's more like it! I'll try it right now.] AI Avatar: Mazaak banwana band karo. Neeche diye gaye link se Speakeasy app abhi install karo. [Stop being a laughing stock. Install the Speakeasy app now from the link below.] Presenter: Abhi Speakeasy app download karein aur farratedar English bolna shuru karein. [Download the Speakeasy app now and start speaking fluent English.]

GET IT ON Google Play. Download on the App Store.
summary: A split-screen ad where a human user makes a literal translation error, and an AI avatar teacher corrects her. The ad promotes Speakeasy as a non-judgmental AI tool to practice English and avoid embarrassing translation mistakes. It ends with a call to download the app.
